core_obligations: Fix a polynomial presentation and restate both sides as module pseudo-coherence.
Transfer between A[x]-module and B-module pseudo-coherence via the finite push lemma.
Apply the two-out-of-three property to the ideal sequence.

proof_roadmap.step: Pushforward transfer plus the short-exact-sequence equivalence.

difficulty_reason: For a flat finitely presented ring map A -> B and an ideal I of B, the lemma says A -> B/I is a pseudo-coherent ring map if and only if I is a pseudo-coherent B-module. The retained proof is written: choose a presentation B = A[x_1,...,x_n]/J; B is pseudo-coherent as an A[x]-module because flat finitely presented maps are pseudo-coherent (chapter lemma flat-finite-presentation-pseudo-coherent, already collected); the ring-map condition for A -> B/I unfolds to B/I being pseudo-coherent as an A[x]-module; the finite pushforward dictionary (More on Algebra, lemma finite-push-pseudo-coherent, applied to the closed immersion Spec B -> Spec A[x]) converts this to B/I pseudo-coherent as a B-module; and the short exact sequence 0 -> I -> B -> B/I -> 0 with B pseudo-coherent (again flat-finite-presentation) and the two-out-of-three property (More on Algebra, lemma two-out-of-three-pseudo-coherent) identifies this with I being pseudo-coherent over B. Retained author proof at lines 17524-17538.
